about: The page's looks, one per power at the setting's table: each a set of role-named tokens the stylesheet and the globe's drawing read, its type, its ornament, and where its colours come from. A theme changes how the page looks, never what it says.

themes.name: The Republic of Letters

home.why: turned to Europe and Africa, where the book starts, and the Indian Ocean beyond, set for Amsterdam's latitude, where Blaeu made his globes

themes.type: 'EB Garamond', 'Euphonia Arabic', 'Euphonia Armenian', 'Euphonia Georgian', 'Euphonia Hebrew', 'Euphonia Devanagari', 'Euphonia Bengali', 'Euphonia Tamil', 'Euphonia Sinhala', 'Euphonia Han', 'Euphonia Hangul', 'Euphonia Khmer', 'Euphonia Lao', 'Euphonia Myanmar', 'Euphonia Ethiopic', 'Euphonia Tibetan', 'Euphonia Thai', 'Euphonia Japanese', serif

provenance.what: type: EB Garamond, roman and italic
provenance.from: Claude Garamont's roman and Robert Granjon's italic as Conrad Berner printed them in the Egenolff–Berner type specimen, Frankfurt, 1592, from which EB Garamond is drawn

source.title: Konrad Berner, Specimen characterum, Cary Graphic Arts Collection, RIT

provenance.what: frame, frame-edge, case, case-edge, paper: the globe's mount and the sheet
provenance.from: Willem Janszoon Blaeu's terrestrial globe, Amsterdam, 1645–48: its brass meridian ring, its wooden horizon and stand, and its printed paper horizon

source.title: Terrestrial globe, Willem Janszoon Blaeu, 1645–48, Rijksmuseum

provenance.from: iron-gall ink, Europe's common writing ink from the fifth century to the nineteenth, brown-black as it ages on paper

source.title: Galling ink! How The National Archives preserves millions of documents written in iron gall ink, The National Archives (UK)

provenance.what: map-empyrean, map-heaven-far, map-heaven-near, map-fire, map-air: the Wheel's spheres, painted
provenance.from: Andreas Cellarius, Scenographia Systematis Mundani Ptolemaici, in Harmonia Macrocosmica (Amsterdam, 1660–61): the Ptolemaic spheres coloured in bands, air and fire about the earth, the planets' spheres in deepening blues, the light of the heavens beyond

source.title: Andreas Cellarius, Scenographia Systematis Mundani Ptolemaici, Christchurch Art Gallery Te Puna o Waiwhetū, 2000/86

provenance.from: the dark ground and warm greys of perceptualmechanics.com's reading pages, which this page grew out of
provenance.authored: Scott Cohen, the parent site's palette

themes.name: Mutapa

home.why: turned to the plateau and set for its latitude, from the stone city whose granite the page is built of

themes.type: 'Alegreya', 'EB Garamond', 'Euphonia Arabic', 'Euphonia Armenian', 'Euphonia Georgian', 'Euphonia Hebrew', 'Euphonia Devanagari', 'Euphonia Bengali', 'Euphonia Tamil', 'Euphonia Sinhala', 'Euphonia Han', 'Euphonia Hangul', 'Euphonia Khmer', 'Euphonia Lao', 'Euphonia Myanmar', 'Euphonia Ethiopic', 'Euphonia Tibetan', 'Euphonia Thai', 'Euphonia Japanese', serif

provenance.what: ornament: the coursings (chevron, herringbone, check, dentelle)
provenance.from: the decorated drystone walls of the plateau: the double chevron of Great Zimbabwe; the check of Khami; Naletale's facade of chevron, herring-bone, check and sloping block, with dark dolerite insets; dentelle and herring-bone at Matendere

source.title: James Walton, Decorative walling and patterned stones (drawing, 1953), James Walton Collection, Stellenbosch University

provenance.what: ornament: where the patterns stand at Great Zimbabwe
provenance.from: the chevron along the top of the Great Enclosure's outer wall
the granite of the plateau's kopjes, whose slabs built Great Zimbabwe without mortar (the book's own Mutapa chapter), laid in the courses above
the copper cross-ingots (croisettes) of south-central Africa, made between the fourteenth and eighteenth centuries, emblems of currency and status

source.title: Stephens, Killick and Chirikure, Reconstructing the geological provenance and long-distance movement of rectangular, fishtail, and croisette copper ingots in Iron Age Zambia and Zimbabwe, PLOS ONE 18(3), 2023

provenance.from: the plateau's gold, which the traders of Benametapa brought down to Sofala

source.title: The Book of Duarte Barbosa, vol. 1 (c. 1518), tr. M. L. Dames, Hakluyt Society, 1918

provenance.what: ground, ink, map-sea and the blues of the globe: blue cloth
provenance.from: the cotton cloths, white and blue, brought to Sofala from Cambay, which Sofala's weavers unravelled and rewove with their own white thread

source.title: The Book of Duarte Barbosa, vol. 1 (c. 1518), tr. M. L. Dames, Hakluyt Society, 1918

provenance.from: machira, the cotton cloth woven in the Rivers of Cuama from cotton grown there

source.title: António da Conceição, Treatise on the Rivers of Cuama (1696), ed. Malyn Newitt, British Academy, 2009

provenance.from: the Indian Ocean glass beads found on Mapungubwe Hill and at K2: red, yellow, green, blue, white, black

source.title: Tournié, Prinsloo and Colomban, Raman classification of the glass beads excavated on Mapungubwe Hill and K2, Journal of Raman Spectroscopy 43(4), 2012

provenance.from: platinum, Mutapa's metal of white fire, from the Great Dyke, the ultramafic ridge down the plateau's spine (the book's Mutapa chapter): its cool grey-white

source.title: Platinum-group elements in southern Africa: mineral inventory and an assessment of undiscovered mineral resources, USGS Scientific Investigations Report 2010-5090-Q

provenance.from: Juan Pablo del Peral's Alegreya (Huerta Tipográfica), a humanist serif for long reading, under the SIL Open Font License
the Zimbabwe soapstone birds, a national emblem carrying ancestral meaning, and the Mapungubwe gold rhinoceros, the emblem of a national order, are not used

source.title: ZIMBABWE SOAPSTONE BIRD, South African Heritage Resources Agency
